Spatial sources in Video32

256 guided tours across 32 reconstructed spaces. All geometry is bundled for offline playback and drawn with the original 32 glyph masks. The point fabrics and camera rails are artistic adaptations, rather than surveys or game simulations.

Mapped geometry © OpenStreetMap contributors, shared under ODbL 1.0. The OSM source subsets and derived fabrics remain available under ODbL in the public repository. This does not change the licences of the other datasets or renderer code.

Kenney City Kit (Suburban) models: CC0. Freedoom level geometry: BSD-3-Clause. United States terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, via Mapzen / Tilezen: public domain, with source and adaptations recorded.

Spherical video studies

256 distinct source videos selected from the UGC360 Dataset, collected by Andy Regensky, Marc Windsheimer, Fabian Brand and André Kaup. UGC360 and the bundled image adaptations are CC BY-SA 4.0. Individual original source licence families are recorded below as supplied by UGC360. Only CC BY, CC BY-SA and CC0 sources were selected; ND and NC sources were excluded.

These are nine-frame studies of 360° equirectangular videos, presented through a 180° hemisphere. Frames are reduced, matched to the exact Video32 masks, colored from image content and bent by music. Source colors are stored as RGB565 before the selected palette treatment. The studies use slow forward/reverse loops and gentle viewing sweeps; they do not reproduce full-length movies or infer 3D depth. The native VR180 dataset located during research was gated and was not bundled.
